full_text_en:
Rui Hua Investment Holding Limited v. Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Co., Ltd., Shandong Jiaxiang Jingwei Copper Co., Ltd., Chen Zhongrong, Gao Xuemin, et al. — dispute over loan and guarantee contracts

【Ruling Summary】

The underlying legal relationship on which the plaintiff bases its action involves multiple loan contracts. Although the borrower is the same entity, the guarantors providing security for these multiple loan contracts are multiple persons, and the objects, amounts, and methods of the guarantees provided by each guarantor are different. According to Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the joinder of such actions requires the consent of the parties and the permission of the people's court; otherwise, the people's court shall not consolidate such cases for trial.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 28

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Rui Hua Investment Holding Limited, domiciled at 10, Frere Felix de Valois Street, Port Louis, Mauritius.

Legal representative: NG Yong Ngee, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Jia Jingchen, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Jiaxiang Jingwei Copper Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Jia Jingchen, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Wolong Agricultural Machinery Repair and Manufacturing Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Mu Qicong, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Jinguan Copper Strip Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: He Jingli, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Tongda Waste Acquisition Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Chen Zhongrong, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Huagui Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd., domiciled at the west side of National Highway 327, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Yue Xicai, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Shandong Huanggang (Group) General Corporation, domiciled at Huanggang Village, Wolongshan Town, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Legal representative: Zhai Genyun, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Jining Longgui Copper Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd., domiciled at Tianchang Building, Ji'anqiao North Road, Jining City.

Legal representative: Lu Guang, Chairman of the board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Chen Zhongrong, residing in the residential compound of Luxiang Group, Jining City.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Gao Xuemin, residing in the residential compound of Luxiang Group, Jining City.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Jia Jingchen, residing at Huoxi West Street, Jiaxiang County, Jining City.

Appellant Rui Hua Investment Holding Limited (hereinafter referred to as Rui Hua Company) appealed to this Court against the civil ruling of the Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the original trial court) (2007) Lu Min Si Chu Zi No. 4-1 in the dispute over loan and guarantee contracts with appellees Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Luxiang Group), Shandong Jiaxiang Jingwei Copper Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingwei Company), Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Wolong Agricultural Machinery Repair and Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Machinery Company), Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Jinguan Copper Strip Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinguan Company), Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Tongda Waste Acquisition Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tongda Company), Shandong Luxiang Copper Group Jiaxiang Huagui Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huagui Company), Shandong Huanggang (Group) General Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Huanggang Group), Jining Longgui Copper Arts and Crafts Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longgui Company), Chen Zhongrong, Gao Xuemin, and Jia Jingchen. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Lu Xiaolong serving as presiding judge, and Judges Chen Jizhong and Xi Xiangyang participating in the deliberation, and has now concluded the trial.

On May 17, 2007, Rui Hua Company filed a lawsuit with the Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the original trial court), alleging: First, Luxiang Group and Jingwei Company owed a principal amount of RMB 13,910,000 in loan principal and corresponding interest, Huanggang Group should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the loan debt, and Chen Zhongrong and Gao Xuemin should each bear joint and several liability for repayment within the scope of the principal amount of RMB 2,010,000 and corresponding interest; Second, Jingwei Company additionally owed a principal amount of RMB 5,000,000 in loan principal and corresponding interest, and Longgui Company should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the loan debt; Third, Luxiang Group additionally owed a principal amount of RMB 10,800,000 in loan principal and corresponding interest, and Huanggang Group should bear joint and several liability for repayment of the loan debt; Fourth, Luxiang Group additionally owed a principal amount of RMB 3,000,000 in loan principal and corresponding interest. On June 25 of the same year, Rui Hua Company withdrew the lawsuit against Jingwei Company and Longgui Company regarding the loan claim of RMB 5,000,000 in principal.

On June 11 of the same year, Huanggang Group, during the period for submitting its statement of defense, raised a jurisdictional objection to the original trial court, stating: First, the total amount in dispute in the lawsuit filed by Rui Hua Company was RMB 32,710,000. According to the relevant provisions on hierarchical jurisdiction published by the original trial court, this case should be accepted by the Jining Intermediate People's Court; Second, before the creditor's rights in this case were transferred to Rui Hua Company, the original creditor, China Orient Asset Management Corporation Qingdao Office, had already filed a lawsuit with the Jining Intermediate People's Court on March 1, 2006, concerning the aforesaid creditor's rights. That court dismissed the lawsuit filed by China Orient Asset Management Corporation Qingdao Office on the ground that the case did not meet the conditions for consolidated trial as required by law. The civil ruling (2006) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 28 of the Jining Intermediate People's Court had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and this effective legal document is binding on this case; Third, if the plaintiff in this case sues all the defendants in this case together, and where the guarantors are not the same entity, a judgment based on the relevant evidence would inevitably lead to unequal protection of the procedural rights of the parties. The plaintiff's filing of the lawsuit against all defendants in the original trial court in a single action does not meet the conditions for necessary joinder as stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The objection requested dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit.

Upon review, the original trial court held: In the lawsuit filed by the plaintiff Rui Hua Company, multiple loan contracts with different amounts were involved. In each loan contract, although the borrower was the same entity, the guarantors and guarantee methods differed, including both legal persons and natural persons, and both guarantees and mortgages. Each was an independent loan contract, involving different legal relationships, and did not constitute a joint action for consolidated trial. The plaintiff should file separate lawsuits based on each loan contract and have them tried separately. Therefore, the plaintiff Rui Hua Company's consolidation of multiple loan contracts in one lawsuit, where the guarantors and guarantee methods differed, did not meet the conditions for necessary joinder as stipulated in Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the original trial court ruled to dismiss the lawsuit filed by Rui Hua Company. The court acceptance fee of RMB 50 was to be borne by Rui Hua Company.

The appellant Rui Hua Company, dissatisfied with the above ruling, appealed to this Court, contending: First, the "consolidated trial" referred to in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) means that a court, on its own authority, consolidates several different cases that have already been separately filed into a single case for trial. In this case, the appellant only filed one case, and there was no issue of consolidated trial. Furthermore, the joint action provided for in Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law merely indicates a form of litigation whose purpose is to clarify the status and rights and obligations of parties in a joint action. The concept of joint action itself is unrelated to the issue of whether a court accepts a case. According to the Civil Procedure Law, a ruling dismissing a lawsuit is only applicable when, after the case is accepted, it is discovered that the plaintiff's lawsuit does not meet the conditions set forth in Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law. The appellant's lawsuit fully satisfied the four conditions specified in Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law. The original trial court's dismissal of the appellant's lawsuit based on Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law constituted an error in the application of law; Second, when the same debtor continuously borrows money from the same creditor within a certain period, for the purpose of saving litigation costs and improving litigation efficiency, it is not contrary to the provisions and purposes of the Civil Procedure Law for the creditor to file a lawsuit on several claims of the same nature as a single aggregate claim. A guarantee contract is an accessory contract. The guarantee contract itself cannot constitute an independent legal relationship and cannot have a material impact on the underlying legal relationship. Regardless of how many guarantors and guarantee methods exist in this dispute, the underlying legal relationship is the loan contract relationship. The appellant's suing of the principal debtor and all guarantors in one action did not infringe upon their procedural rights. The principal debtor and each guarantor still had the right to exercise their own defenses, and any party dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment could file an appeal. Therefore, the procedural legal status of the appellant and all appellees was completely equal; Third, given the specific circumstances of this case, the original trial court should not have simply dismissed the appellant's lawsuit. In judicial practice in recent years, it has been common for various asset management companies, in the process of recovering non-performing loans, to sue on several loans in a single action. The original trial court itself had heard many cases of the same nature as this one and had rendered judgments on the merits. The appellant, referring to the acceptance practice of the original trial court, filed the lawsuit in this manner. The appellant had taken various litigation measures based on the trial practice of the original trial court, but these measures would create difficulties for the realization of the appellant's claims due to the original trial court's simplistic approach of dismissing the lawsuit. Request: 1. To overturn the civil ruling (2007) Lu Min Chu Zi No. 41 of the original trial court and to direct the original trial court to continue the trial of this case; 2. To order the appellees to bear the costs of this appeal.

The appellees Luxiang Group, Jingwei Company, Agricultural Machinery Company, Jinguan Company, Tongda Company, Huagui Company, Huanggang Group, Longgui Company, Chen Zhongrong, Gao Xuemin, and Jia Jingchen did not submit any statement of defense.

This Court holds: The underlying legal relationship on which the appellant Rui Hua Company bases its lawsuit involves multiple loan contracts. The borrowers are Luxiang Group and Jingwei Company. The guarantors providing security for the loan contracts include multiple natural persons and multiple legal persons. The objects, amounts, and methods of the guarantees provided by each guarantor are different. According to Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the joinder of such actions requires the consent of the parties and the permission of the people's court. In this case, Huanggang Group, as one of the parties, explicitly raised a jurisdictional objection to the lawsuit filed by the appellant Rui Hua Company in the original trial court and did not consent to a consolidated trial. The original trial court also did not consider that this case could be tried in a consolidated manner. Therefore, the lawsuit filed by the appellant in the original trial court did not meet the statutory conditions for consolidated trial. The appellant's appeal is without merit and should be dismissed in accordance with the law.

In summary, the ruling of the original trial court contains no error in the determination of facts or the application of law and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1(1), and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

Appeal dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Lu Xiaolong

Judge: Chen Jizhong

Judge: Xi Xiangyang

April 21, 2008
